title: Reuse connections with requests.Session and add a timeout
summary: Fold repeated requests.get calls into one Session, pass a timeout so the job cannot hang, and stop on every error except 404 with raise_for_status.

files.content:
import requests

API_URL = "https://api.example.com"


def fetch_orders(token, order_ids):
    orders = []
    for order_id in order_ids:
        response = requests.get(
            f"{API_URL}/orders/{order_id}",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
        )
        orders.append(response.json())
    return orders

turns.user: batch job pulls 500 orders from the orders api. slow, and sometimes it just sits there until morning

assistant.body: TL;DR: two separate problems. requests.get builds a throwaway Session on every call, so all 500 requests open a fresh TCP and TLS connection. A requests.Session keeps the connection to the same host and reuses it. The other one is the timeout. By default requests waits forever, so a server that goes quiet stalls the job until someone kills it. A tuple sets the connect and read limits separately. Note: a Session cannot hold a timeout, so it goes on every call.

import requests

API_URL = "https://api.example.com"
TIMEOUT = (3.05, 10)


def fetch_orders(token, order_ids):
    orders = []
    with requests.Session() as session:
        session.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        for order_id in order_ids:
            response = session.get(f"{API_URL}/orders/{order_id}", timeout=TIMEOUT)
            orders.append(response.json())
    return orders

turns.user: way faster. but deleted orders come back as {"error": "not found"} and land in orders, then the report dies with KeyError. skip 404s, stop on anything else

assistant.body: Sure. requests does not raise on a 4xx or 5xx, so the error body was treated as a normal order. This skips 404 first and lets raise_for_status turn everything else into an HTTPError. In other words, only a 2xx body can end up in orders.
